summary:
Orbvital is an autonomous crew health monitoring, contactless vision biometrics, and radiation triage platform built for astronauts and non-medical crewmates on deep-space missions, where Earth communication delays reach 23 minutes one-way and solar conjunctions cause 2 to 3 week blackouts.

Instead of replacing Earth flight surgeons or relying on unverified generative AI, Orbvital follows one core principle: "Rules decide, AI advises." A deterministic decision engine grounded in NASA-STD-3001 and the NASA HRP 5 spaceflight hazards evaluates 7 physiological vitals across 4 flight phases (1-G, Ascent, 0-G, EDL) and 5 habitats (Spacecraft, Station, Rover, Lunar Base, Mars Base), while Gemini provides a plain-language second opinion.

Using MediaPipe and FER+ ONNX computer vision, Orbvital identifies crew members without physical contact, detects incapacitation, and enables Buddy Input Mode for rapid crew-assisted triage. Results are visualized on an interactive 5-zone 3D Digital Twin with a What-If Dock to simulate shielding and countermeasures risk-free. Integrated with live NOAA SWPC solar storm scales and NASA DONKI CME forecasts, Orbvital delivers early radiation triage alerts so crews can act autonomously when Earth cannot respond.
details:
Orbvital — Autonomous Deep-Space Crew Health, Vision Biometrics & Radiation Triage What does it do and how does it work? Orbvital is an autonomous crew health monitoring, contactless biometrics, and radiation triage platform built for deep-space, long-duration missions (Lunar transit/bases and Mars transit/bases) where Earth communication delays reach up to 23 minutes one-way and solar conjunctions can cause 2–3 week communication blackouts. It combines four integrated layers:

  1. Contactless Vision Biometrics & Buddy Triage: Using computer vision (MediaPipe and FER+ ONNX via FastAPI), Orbvital identifies crew members without physical contact, estimates emotional/fatigue state, and detects incapacitation. In emergencies, Buddy Input Mode allows any non-medical crewmate to log symptoms and perform rapid step-by-step triage.
  2. Interactive 3D Digital Twin & 5-Habitat Calibration: Built with Three.js and React Three Fiber, the 3D Digital Twin maps 7 physiological vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, SpO2, sleep, and mood) into 5 anatomical zones (Heart, Brain & Mood, Blood & Respiration, Bones & Muscles, Sleep) across 5 operational habitats (SPACECRAFT, STATION, ROVER, LUNAR_BASE, MARS_BASE). It also includes a What-If Dock for risk-free simulation of shielding postures, solar storms, and countermeasures.
  3. Mission-Aware Trajectory & Space-Weather Radiation Triage: Orbvital tracks mission flight phases (1-G, Ascent, 0-G, EDL) alongside live NOAA SWPC solar radiation storm scales (S0–S5) and NASA DONKI CME/WSA-ENLIL forecasts to issue early warnings and classify crew into actionable triage bands (EVA hold vs. mandatory STORM_SHELTER ingress and increased vital monitoring cadence).
  4. "Rules Decide, AI Advises" Decision Engine: A deterministic rule engine grounded in NASA-STD-3001 and the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) 5 spaceflight hazards makes all safety-critical verdicts (Continue, Caution / Monitor, Execute Contingency). Gemini (@google/genai) acts strictly as a second opinion to explain clinical context in plain language for non-medical crewmates. What benefits does it have and what is its intended impact?
  • Medical Autonomy Beyond LEO: Closes the critical care gap when Mission Control flight surgeons cannot respond in real time due to latency or solar blackouts.
  • Zero-Friction Crew Workflows: Reduces manual logging burden during routine operations and empowers non-physician crewmates to act decisively during incapacitation or radiation events.
  • Certifiable Safety by Design: Separating deterministic NASA-backed rules from generative AI prevents hallucinations from driving life-critical decisions while maintaining full auditability and asynchronous Earth sync once signal returns.
  • Dual-Use Terrestrial Impact: Beyond Artemis/Mars crews and commercial space habitats, the same not earth-dependent-first triage architecture applies to submarines, Antarctic stations, offshore rigs, mining sites, and remote rural clinics without continuous connectivity. Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used
  • Frontend: TypeScript, Next.js 14, React 18, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei), Lucide Icons.
  • Backend & Persistence: TypeScript, Node.js, Express, Prisma ORM, PostgreSQL, Zod, JWT, Bcrypt, Vitest, Gemini API (@google/genai).
  • Computer Vision Service: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, OpenCV (opencv-python-headless), MediaPipe, ONNX Runtime (FER+), NumPy, SciPy, WebSockets, Pytest.
  • Scientific & Telemetry Sources: NASA HRP 5-hazard framework and NASA-STD-3001 physiological norms, NOAA SWPC solar radiation feeds, and NASA DONKI CME analysis feeds (with local nominal fallbacks for not earth-dependent operation).
  • Hardware & Deployment: Runs on standard workstation/onboard compute with a standard RGB camera/webcam (no proprietary medical sensors required); deployed with Vercel, Render, and Docker. How is it creative and what factors did our team consider?
  • Creativity: Instead of building another passive vital-signs dashboard or letting an LLM act as an autonomous doctor, we unified contactless vision, 3D anatomical visualization, live space-weather and trajectory context, and a What-If countermeasure simulator under one core philosophy: "Rules decide, AI advises."
  • Target Scope: Designed specifically for astronauts and non-medical crewmates in communication-denied deep-space environments—not as a consumer fitness app or replacement for Earth flight surgeons.
  • Not earth-dependent Resilience: Deterministic rules, vision inference, and nominal radiation fallbacks operate locally without requiring continuous Earth internet.
  • Human Factors & Cognitive Load: Color-coded 5-zone 3D triage and plain-language explanations reduce cognitive overload during high-stress emergencies.
